text.p: In overnight commodity markets, zinc prices probed new 4 1/2 year lows before bouncing back, while gold prices lifted with platinum prices.
Oil prices fell back on talk of Iraqi supply, while wheat prices were helped higher soybean prices.
The CRB index fell 0.36 points to a New York close of 246.64.
Short-covering helped to lift base metals by the close of London Metal Exchange business on Thursday, a move that may spark further gains near-term if overhead resistance levels are breached.

Zinc probed 4-1/2 year lows, nickel found support from a strike at Inco, while aluminium clawed towards the $1,600 level. Investment fund buying and short-covering after a recent corrective pull back propelled zinc higher. Traders said the market was gaining in upside confidence after expected Chinese deliveries into LME warehouses failed to materialise.

Last zinc business was at $1,375, a $25 gain from Wednesday's close. The strike at Inco Sudbury continued to underpin nickel which finished $40 higher at $7,240. Traders noted news that gas supplies at Norilsk nickel main production complex have been cut by nearly one third.
Aluminium moved to test $1,600, though overhead selling was capping further gains up to resistance placed at $1,610 and $1,620.
Traders said they expected the market to consolidate after recent LME stock falls. Last business was at $1,600, up $8. Copper remained quiet and was last at $2,481, up $3.
CBOT soft red winter wheat futures ended higher on Thursday, lifted by late gains in soybeans and by perceptions the market had already put in harvest lows, pit sources said.
Harvest in Texas hard red winter was said to be progressing quickly but cash sources gave mixed reviews to early yields and quality. Lackluster weekly USDA export sales pressured the market early.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture put net old and new crop wheat sales at 423,600 tonnes. That estimate fell below trade expectations for sales of 500,000 to 700,000 tonnes. The International Grains Council upped its estimate for China wheat production to 112 million tonnes and said China's imports would fall by three million tonnes to four million. CBOT SRW wheat ended 3-1/4 to 1-3/4 cents per bushel higher with July up 2-1/4 at $3.56.

NYMEX crude ended lower for the third consecutive session Thursday as increasing domestic supply and the prospect of $2 billion worth of Iraqi oil for another six months continued to weigh on the market."There is a general sense that storage levels are rising and that crude does not deserve a premium given the supply situation," said Mike De Luca, trader with Prudential Securities. July crude settled off 46 cents at $19.66 a barrel.

COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended higher Thursday, led by gains in platinum prices, amid ongoing talk of delivery problems in the physical market, due to a five month suspension of exports by Russia, the world's largest supplier of platinum group metals (PGMs). COMEX August gold ended up $2.00 an ounce at $345.60, while in the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $343.10/60, compared to the London Thursday afternoon fix at $340.80 and the New York close Wednesday around $341.00/50.
